title: Annotatio VI §.IV: seeming proof from Fathers — hear Augustine interpret his own metonymy
pass_a_gloss: And after he had recited some such testimonies of Augustine and of other Fathers, he continues: I beseech you, do not the unfaithful and Unworthy seem from these testimonies to feed on Christ’s body? But now let us hear Augustine himself interpreting himself and his Metonymy.
pass_b_english: After listing Augustine and other Fathers in that vein, Picherellus asks: don’t the unfaithful and unworthy seem, from these texts, to feed on Christ’s body?
Answer: hear Augustine interpret his own metonymy.
source_text: Et postquam Augustini, aliorumque Patrum nonnulla hujusmodi testimonia recitasset, pergit: Obsecro Te, nonne ex his testimoniis, infideles & Indigni videntur Christi vesci corpore? At verò ipsum jam audiamus Augustinum, se suámque Metonymiam interpretantem.
